seo.description: Complete guide to Biomedical Engineering (PG) in Ireland for Indian students: Top Irish universities, eligibility criteria, tuition fees (€13,500 – €28,640 / year), scholarships, and 2-year post-study work visa (Stamp 1G).

sections.title: 1. Why Study Biomedical Engineering in Ireland?

items: Ireland’s medical device, healthcare technology and life sciences industries make it an attractive destination to study postgraduate Biomedical Engineering. The field integrates engineering, biology and medicine to create technologies that aid in the diagnosis, treatment and monitoring of medical conditions.
A postgraduate qualification can help students to develop skills in biomechanics, medical device design, biomaterials, medical electronics and biomedical research.
Why Study Biomedical Engineering in Ireland?
Access to specialist programs in *Biomedical Engineering and Medical Technology.
Opportunities to undertake research projects related to real health care problems.
Exposure to *medical device design, manufacturing and quality systems.
Career paths in research and development, product design, manufacturing and regulatory affairs.
Opportunities to specialize in medical electronics, tissue engineering, computational modeling and healthcare innovation.
Edu Hawk worldwide study abroad guidance helps students to explore these opportunities and know the requirements involved in pursuing education overseas.

sections.title: 2. Courses in Biomedical Engineering in Ireland

items: Postgraduate Biomedical Engineering programs in Ireland might be offered as a Master of Science (MSc), Master of Engineering (ME) or other relevant postgraduate qualification.
Typical areas of study:
- Design of biomedical devices -
Biomechanics & Computational Biomechanics
- Tissue engineering and biomaterials
- Bioinstrumentation and medical electronics
- Medical imaging and signal processing
- Medical Device Manufacturing
- Numerical modeling and finite element analysis
- Healthcare technology & innovation
- Research methods and projects of biomedical engineering
Some programs have a focus on technical specialization and research, others are aimed at advanced engineering practice.
If you are a student, who is interested to design electronic healthcare equipment, you should look for medical electronics modules.
If you are interested in implants and biological materials , the fields of biomaterials and tissue engineering .

sections.title: 4. Eligibility for Study Biomedical Engineering in Ireland

items: Applicants will normally require a recognized -
Bachelor’s degree in Biomedical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Electronic Engineering or other relevant engineering discipline.

The minimum academic requirement for the University of Galway's MSc in Biomedical Engineering is a Second Class Honors, Grade 1 (H2.1) in a Level 8 engineering degree in a related discipline or its equivalent.
The university will look at the content of the undergraduate degree, especially previous learning in engineering, mathematics and physics.
Academic performance and the availability of places will be taken into account.
Typical eligibility considerations are-
Related engineering or technical degree
Satisfactory academic performance.
Knowledge of *basics of mathematics, physics and engineering
Proficiency in English language, where applicable.
Relevant academic projects or experience, if asked.

sections.title: 5. Admission requirements for Biomedical Engineering Eligibility in Ireland

items: Universities will usually look at academic qualifications, previous subject knowledge and English language proficiency.
Typical admission requirements include:
Bachelor’s degree certificate* or provisional certificate.
Official mark sheets and academic transcripts.
Evidence of English proficiency (if applicable).
CV or résumé if requested.
Statement of purpose*, if applicable.
References* (academic/professional) where required. - Research details, projects or relevant work experience (if applicable).

Minimum standard English language requirements: The following English language profile is required for the University of Galway MSc in Biomedical Engineering: IELTS 6.5 overall with 6.5 in writing and 6.0 in each other skill (or accepted equivalent)
Applicants should describe their previous studies in relation to biomedical engineering and explain their interests such as in medical devices, biomechanics, biomaterials or medical electronics.

sections.title: 6. Cost of Studying Biomedical Engineering in Ireland

items: The overall cost of studying consists of tuition fees, accommodation, food, transport, health insurance, study materials and personal expenses.
For the University of Galway the published fees for the 2026/27 academic year are:
MSc Biomedical Engineering - €28,640*
ME Biomedical Engineering - €28,640
The MSc fee is €28,500 tuition fee plus €140 levy.
Other expenses to plan for are:
- Room and utilities
Food and groceries
- Public transit
- Medical insurance
- Visa and immigration expenses, where applicable
*Books equipment and personal expenses

Accommodation is often a major expense, so compare student housing and private rental options before choosing a university. Research scholarships and funding opportunities early and make sure to check eligibility conditions before adding any potential award to your budget.

items: 8\. Accreditation and Recognition

Professional recognition Accreditation are important things to consider when considering an engineering qualification. But the status of a program depends on the exact degree, course structure and relevant accreditation requirements.
Check before you accept an offer:
If the program is accredited.
Which professional body or accreditation framework is applicable
If the accreditation covers your intended intake.
If the degree meets the educational requirements for your intended professional engineering stream.
If extra qualifications or relevant professional experience are necessary.
Engineers Ireland has information on accredited engineering programs and professional recognition.

sections.title: 9. Career Opportunities and Salary after Biomedical Engineering in Ireland

items: Biomedical Engineering graduates are employed in medical devices, healthcare technology, pharmaceuticals, research and advanced manufacturing.
Job opportunities will depend on technical specialization, experience, employer requirements and market conditions.
Possible job titles are :
- Engineer Biomedicine
Design Engineer
Medical Devices*
- Research and Development Engineer
- Medical Devices Electronics Engineer
- Bio-mechanical engineer
- Manufacturing Engineer
- Quality Assurance (QA) Engineer
- Design Assurance Engineer
- Regulatory Affairs Associate / Specialist
*Biomedical R\&D Engineer
Salary ranges will vary by position and experience.

Graduate roles are often very different to senior engineering and specialist roles, so compare current Irish vacancies for the role you’re interested in, rather than just relying on one salary estimate.

Useful skills could include CAD, finite element analysis, medical device design, electronics, data analysis, testing and validation, quality systems and regulatory documentation. The most valuable skills are different for each role.

faqs.q: Q.1 Is Ireland a good place to do a post graduate in Biomedical Engineering?
faqs.a: Ireland is a good choice for students interested in biomedical research and innovation in engineering, medical devices, healthcare technology. The best choice depends on the modules, costs, entry requirements and career goals of the program.

faqs.q: Q2. Which Irish University offers MSc in Biomedical Engineering?
faqs.a: The University of Galway offers a full-time one-year MSc in Biomedical Engineering. It also has a separate ME in Biomedical Engineering but you should check the eligibility requirements for each route.

faqs.q: Q3. What is the Tuition Fee for Biomedical Engineering PG in Ireland?
faqs.a: The University of Galway has announced the total non-EU fee at €28,640 for its MSc and ME Biomedical Engineering programs for 2026/ 27. Additional living costs will be incurred and fees may vary in future years.

faqs.q: Q4. Are Electrical/Mechanical Engineering students eligible to apply?
faqs.a: Yes, potentially. Other engineering backgrounds may be acceptable depending on the prerequisites of the program and what your bachelors covers . Before you apply, contact the university to check your eligibility.

faqs.q: Q5. What are the career opportunities after a master’s in Biomedical Engineering?
faqs.a: Possible career paths include biomedical engineer, medical device design engineer, research and development engineer, manufacturing engineer, quality engineer and regulatory affairs specialist. Your employment will depend on your skills, experience, employer needs and applicable work-permission rules.
